source.title: Instance-Dependent Early Stopping for Adaptive Data Pruning
source.authors: Su-Qin Yuan; Runqi Lin; Felix Azian; Lei Feng; Bo Han; Gang Niu; Masashi Sugiyama; Tong-Liang Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices. Its header identifies it as an ICLR 2025 conference paper, despite the supplied TPAMI 2026 title metadata.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares instance-dependent sample removal with full-data training and reports test error, training loss, and sharpness measures. These results bear on the broader generalization-gap subject, but do not test any listed version's specific intervention or measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for instance-dependent early stopping, including comparisons of test error, training loss, gradient norm, SAM value, and maximum Hessian eigenvalue. Its random-removal and other sample-selection comparisons are included only where they report the outcome of a removal method. Cited prior work is not extracted.
record.test_reason: Table 1 incidentally bears on V4: under the default CIFAR architectures, it reports held-out accuracy for AdamW and several SGD schedules, both with full-data training and IES. These comparisons were omitted from the record. The extracted Figure 4 rows themselves test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that IES reduces computation while generally preserving model performance and transferability, and report faster reductions in training loss and measured sharpness. These are empirical method-performance findings; they do not establish V7's sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes instance-dependent early stopping based on second-order loss differences, with reversible exclusion from backpropagation; it does not use the original claim's interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, optimizer, stopping threshold, and the amount of backpropagation saved vary across experiments. The Figure 4 comparison reports results for SGD and Adam separately.

fits_no_version.finding: At equal backpropagation counts, IES reportedly lowers test error, training loss, fixed-radius SAM, and maximum Hessian eigenvalue, while increasing selected-batch gradient norms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reversibly skipping mastered examples can improve training efficiency and held-out performance relative to full-data training at equal backpropagation counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Under 10% label noise on CIFAR-100, IES maintains comparable best accuracy while saving backpropagation in epoch-wise double-descent settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instance-dependent early stopping can preserve performance when noisy-label training continues through epoch-wise double descent.

record.problems: Figure 4 values are presented as plots without extractable numbers in the supplied text. The paper says Figure 4 uses 5 runs, mean±std, but the figure descriptions do not give uncertainty values. The reported comparison does not establish that sharpness causes or reliably predicts the generalization gap.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting and natural-versus-random held-out comparison; partial label-noise experiments do not establish this version.
No width sweep past interpolation. Appendix G studies epoch-wise double descent, which varies training duration rather than width.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or intervention on local connectivity.
No documented optimizer tuning search, matched training-performance comparison, language benchmark, Adam-to-SGD switch, or controlled test of decoupled weight decay against coupled weight decay.
No dropout intervention; dropout is omitted throughout.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measure, matched-low-training-loss comparison, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison against norm and margin measures.
No inclusion-influence memorization scores, removal of the most memorized examples, or retraining against equal random removal. IES reversibly skips examples during training.

missing.what: Add cross-optimizer test-accuracy comparisons for the default ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and ResNet-34 on CIFAR-100. Record AdamW versus each SGD schedule separately for No Removal and IES, including reported standard deviations. These comparisons support the V4 verdicts; Figure 4's within-optimizer rows cannot substitute for them.
missing.locator: Table 1 optimizer block; Appendix A default architectures; Appendix B.3 optimizer settings

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text identifies Instance-dependent Early Stopping, arXiv:2502.07547, as an ICLR 2025 paper; its identity does not match the supplied TPAMI DOI metadata. V4 evidence is incidental and restricted to the reported fixed recipes: the paper does not document the optimizer tuning protocol needed to reproduce the original limited-tuning comparison. All ten extracted rows also omit Figure 4's batch size 128 and threshold 1e-4. Their qualitative directions are supported by the caption and Section 3.3, but numerical plot values are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test performance.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width required to fit the data.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD for generalization.

The paper measures SAM values and maximum Hessian eigenvalues alongside performance, but does not test magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness across networks at similarly low training loss or compare it with norm- and margin-based measures.
No identification and removal of the most memorized examples followed by retraining; IES dynamically stops backpropagation on instances based on loss differences.
